Mira (CS): Customer 'AcmeCorp' reporting repeated 403s when calling hosted inference (/v1/generate). They say embeddings calls succeed but generation fails. Copying the payload and error they sent.

Customer: `curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-XXXX" -d '{"model":"fast-chat-1","input":"Hello"}'`

Response: `HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden`
`{ "error": { "code": 403, "message": "token missing required scope: generation" } }`

Alex (CS): Do we know whether that key was created by SSO/SCIM or via the org UI?

Mira (CS): Looks like SCIM-provisioned service key. Audit shows creation on 2024-11-03T19:02:14Z by scim-bot with scopes: `embeddings.read, rerank.write` (no generation/stream). Audit id: `audit_20241103_6721`.

Sam (Eng): That matches an edge case I saw in PROV-482 where the SCIM mapping for service_accounts strips inference scopes when team_role == `viewer`. We didn't catch it in the last release.

Mira (CS): Customer asked for repro steps so they can validate after we patch. Suggested curl to check scopes: 
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-XXXX" \\n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/keys/me 
```
Expect: `{"key":{"id":"...","scopes":["generation","embeddings","rerank"]}}`

Sam (Eng): Immediate workaround: create a short-lived support key with the missing scopes and share with the customer (rotate afterwards). Example: `redwoodctl keys create --org acme --scopes generation,embeddings,rerank --expires 2h`

Eve (Security): If we change the provisioner behavior, we need to ensure we don't auto-grant generation for keys that explicitly request only embeddings. Propose: preserve requested scopes from SCIM mapping, and add an explicit test to fail when a service-account mapping strips known inference scopes.

Sam (Eng): I'll push a canary fix to the provisioner to stop trimming the `generation` and `stream` scopes for service_account type. ETA ~2h for canary. Assigning review to @Eve for policy check.

Mira (CS): Shared the audit id with the customer. They prefer staged fix + temporary key rather than full rotation. Creating support ticket and will issue the short-lived key now.

deploy-bot: prov-service: release v1.4.3 -> v1.4.4 (canary) — deployment started

Sam (Eng): Patch includes: 1) fix to SCIM scope mapping, 2) unit test for service_account mappings, 3) post-deploy alert to monitor spikes in 403s. If canary looks good we'll roll to prod.

Mira (CS): Customer accepted the temporary key and validated generation calls work. I left instructions: rotate the original SCIM key after we confirm prod roll.

Sam (Eng): Will follow up with a short runbook for CS: how to validate key scopes, where to find audit ids, and the redwoodctl command. If we see other tenants hit this, we should treat as P1 until we confirm triggering condition.

Eve (Security): Agreed. Please tag me on the postmortem.

Mira (CS): Closing loop with customer in the ticket; will update when prod roll is complete.
